doc.title: Wendy Oxenhorn interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 22, 2026

title: Closing tribute and appeal for the Foundation
summary: Monk wraps up with the Imperioli quote, and she urges donations and names Roberta Flack, Sinead O'Connor and Abbey Lincoln among those helped.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: You must really sleep well at night, Wendy, and I’d like to wrap this up with an observation and then a quote. Usually when I research for an interview and I look up a musician’s information there’ll be lists of, let’s say Milt Hinton, you know and they’ll list all the records he played on and all this. And a discography so to speak. Well you have your own discography with the recognitions and the awards that you have received, and I’m extremely impressed by what you’ve done. I never thought I would be quoting an actor from the Sopranos in an interview but you’re probably familiar with this quote from Michael Imperioli who said, “Wendy gets an immense amount of joy from helping people. I’m a Buddhist. In my religion we call that a “bodhisattva” – somebody who actually dedicates their lives to serving and helping others. That’s who she is.” So thank you for being who you are and taking the time out today to share it with us.

Thank you, thank you for doing this, and for all the archives I’ve been watching and they’ve been incredible. You get moments of people where you don’t usually see who they are. And I just did want to say that for anyone watching who has money to donate, please give to the Jazz Foundation of America. You know every time a musician calls me and something is happening, they’ll pay their rent. People that, I mean oh my goodness you know we never say who we help because there are pride issues but there are musicians that said publicly who we helped so I can say Roberta Flack, Sinead O’Connor, you know, Abby Lincoln. And you can only imagine the level of people we helped who didn’t say it publicly. So I just want to say please give to the Jazz Foundation, Joe Petrucelli and the gang are doing an amazing job keeping it up. The money needs to come in in order to keep helping and they are helping. You know all those numbers of musicians and still with the same – I know Alisa, I don’t know the other social workers anymore but Alisa is a very loving spirit you know. So please help continue to make it possible for these people who gave us so much beauty and are very proud people who never, still to this day very rarely ask for help for themselves.
All right. Thank you so much.
